title: I was paid to write fake Google reviews – then my ‘bosses’ tried to scam me | Scams | The Guardian

facts.fact: The article's scammer recruiter promised that the fake-review job could pay up to £800 a day, a claim the reporter set out to test; this is the scammers' promise, not a verified payment rate.
facts.quote: This time I decided to see whether the promises of up to £800 a day were true.

facts.fact: According to the reporter, two or three offers of work to write fake reviews arrived per month on Telegram, because their number was on a list of potential targets.
facts.quote: so two or three offers of work come through a month.

facts.fact: The reporter says that after responding, nine days of prodding, coaching and motivational messages followed to persuade them to sign up for the job.
facts.quote: nine days of prodding, coaching and motivational messages followed to try to persuade me to sign up for the job.

facts.fact: The Guardian article says fake customer reviews cost consumers billions of pounds a year in misdirected spending; this is the author's characterisation rather than a sourced figure.
facts.quote: costing consumers billions of pounds a year in misdirected spending

facts.fact: A fraud consultant quoted on the page says online scam volume has increased substantially over the last six or seven years.
facts.quote: A fraud consultant says there has seen a big increase in the volume of online scams in the last six or seven years.

facts.fact: The scammers paid the reporter in USDC, which the article describes as a stablecoin pegged to the US dollar.
facts.quote: accepting payments in USDC, a stablecoin that is pegged to the US dollar.

facts.fact: The article states that under UK law, recipients of cryptocurrency payments must declare their source.
facts.quote: (Under UK law recipients of cryptocurrency payments must declare their source.

facts.fact: The article page is marked as more than 7 months old at the time of capture, with a publication date of 27 March 2026.
facts.quote: This article is more than 7 months old

facts.fact: The Guardian's linked related article reports that five firms, including Autotrader and Just Eat, were investigated over fake review failings.
facts.quote: Five firms including Autotrader and Just Eat investigated over fake review failings
